description: Shared Renovate preset for yschimke Android / Compose / Kotlin repos. Updates are clustered by release train (things that share a version and are ABI-coupled move together); everything else stays small. Extend with { "extends": ["github>yschimke/renovate-config"] }.

packageRules.description: A -SNAPSHOT is never an upgrade target. Renovate's gradle versioning ranks `1.0.0-SNAPSHOT` ABOVE `1.0.0-alpha18`, so an upstream that publishes snapshots into a repository the build already reads is offered as if it were a release — rc-players is currently offered `androidx.compose.remote:* 1.0.0-alpha18 -> 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT` on seven coordinates at once. Filtering the suffix out of the candidate list rather than disabling the update keeps the next genuine release on offer, and leaves a repo that deliberately sits ON a snapshot where it is. A repo-local rule that sets `allowedVersions` for the whole gradle manager REPLACES this one for those deps — last match wins on the same field — so such a rule has to carry the suffix itself.

Ignore the legacy-API -compat artifacts (e.g. kotlinx-datetime 0.8.0-0.6.x-compat). Carries the -SNAPSHOT filter from the rule above as well: both set `allowedVersions` and the last match wins, so naming only -compat here would hand kotlinx its snapshots back.

Auto-land patch & minor updates once every CI check on the branch is green. platformAutomerge is false, so Renovate waits for ALL checks (not just branch-protection-required ones) before merging — it cannot merge ahead of CI. A grouped PR only automerges if every update in it qualifies, so any group that happens to contain a major stays manual. To switch to instant GitHub-native merge instead, set platformAutomerge:true here and mark the CI checks required on main via branch protection.
Kotlin compiler train: stdlib, the Kotlin Gradle plugins, the Compose compiler plugin, and KSP all track the compiler version and must bump together.
kotlinx libraries (coroutines, serialization, io, datetime) release independently of the compiler but are co-tested; batch them to cut PR noise.
JetBrains Compose Multiplatform release train plus its lifecycle / navigation companions, which version in lockstep with it.

Catch-all for the remaining, independently-versioned AndroidX libraries (core, activity, datastore, work, navigation3, test, ...). Batched because these small libs rarely break; the release-train groups below deliberately override this for their members.
AndroidX Compose (BOM-aligned) artifacts move together. Overrides the androidx catch-all.
Wear Compose / TV plus Horologist, which tracks the Wear Compose line. Overrides the androidx catch-all.
Room + SQLite + the Room Gradle plugin move together and are KSP-coupled. Overrides the androidx catch-all.
gRPC + protobuf runtime/codegen must move in lockstep.

yschimke/compose-ai-tools ships the preview CLI, the `ee.schimke.composeai.preview` Gradle plugin, the discovery / bundle / render-session / render-host artifacts, its own `*-preview-runtime` modules and the reusable CI actions as ONE release, so a pinned action ref and the Gradle coords must move in a single PR — a skew breaks preview discovery outright. This is the BROAD rule for the `ee.schimke.composeai` group, and the FOUR rules after it carve their own trains back out of it; the last match wins, so they stay after it. The annotation, connector, data and renderer artifacts this train used to ship are no longer part of it — they moved to yschimke/compose-preview-daemon at its 3.0.0 (compose-ai-tools#5336) and are carved out immediately below.

yschimke/compose-preview-daemon — the renderers, the data extractors, the render daemon and the preview runtimes it hosts. The fifth train under this group, and the one the split left behind: these coordinates moved out of compose-ai-tools at the daemon's 3.0.0 (compose-ai-tools#5336) onto a 3.x line of their own, but no rule followed them, so every one of them fell into the compose-ai-tools group above. rc-players is currently offered `fix(deps): update compose-ai-tools to v3.4.3` for two daemon artifacts, and compose-preview-server has the tools line and the daemon line riding one PR. Listed by exact artifactId, like the contracts and the server, because the names interleave three ways: `data-render-compose` is the daemon's but `data-render-core` is a contract, and `slot-preview-runtime` is the daemon's but `wear-preview-runtime` is compose-ai-tools'. Regenerate the list from that repository with `grep -rhA2 '^  coordinates($' --include=build.gradle.kts . | grep -o '"[a-z0-9-]*"'`; a newly published coordinate has to be added by hand or it falls back into compose-ai-tools.

yschimke/compose-preview-contracts — the published wire contracts. They carry the `ee.schimke.composeai` group but are released from their own repository on their own version line (2.x, while compose-ai-tools is on 1.5x.x), so they must not ride the compose-ai-tools group: one group means one shared version ref, and Renovate would raise it to a version the other train never published. Listed by exact artifactId because the two repos' names interleave — `daemon-protocol` is a contract and `daemon-core` is not, `data-render-core` is a contract and `data-render-compose` is not. `screen-document`, `ui-builder-protocol` and `parity-issues-protocol` were missing from this list while three catalogs already resolved them on the shared `composeai-contracts` ref, so they fell into the compose-ai-tools group: that is how compose-preview-daemon#91 (“update compose-ai-tools to v2.17.0”) and #92 (“update compose-preview-contracts to v2.17.0”) ended up as two branches with byte-identical diffs, both rewriting the same version ref.

yschimke/compose-preview-server — `compose-preview serve` and its render host. Same group coordinate, own repository, own version line again, independent of both compose-ai-tools and the contracts. `compose-preview-ui-builder-export` is the third and was the one missing: wear-m3-catalog resolves it on a `composePreviewServer` ref of its own and it was landing in the compose-ai-tools group. If the server publishes more, add them here rather than letting them fall back into the compose-ai-tools group.

yschimke/rc-players — the RemoteCompose players, the fourth train under this group and the one that proved the point. Grouped with compose-ai-tools, Renovate raised a shared version ref to a player-only version and dragged four compose-ai-tools artifacts to a version nobody published (wear-m3-catalog#199).
Give majors extra soak time before opening the PR.
